title: Concern: possible retaliation after security report — investigation logistics & privacy safeguards
text:
Concern: possible retaliation after security report — investigation logistics & privacy safeguards

["From: Beth King <beth.king@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Concern: possible retaliation after security report

Hannah,

I'm reaching out from BrightPath Health. We have an active engagement with Redwood and there was an incident yesterday where our deployment lead raised a concern about data access. After filing a formal question via the project Slack thread, our POC (Anya Petrov) reports that their Redwood contact, Rishi Malhotra, removed their workspace access and made several comments implying there would be consequences for escalation.

This feels like retaliation. We need this handled discreetly — Anya is worried about losing access to critical logs. Could you confirm you received this and advise what steps Redwood will take to preserve evidence and protect our contact from retaliation?

I've attached a screenshot of the Slack exchange and the timestamped access denial.

Thanks,

Beth King
Head of Vendor Relations
BrightPath Health
Attachments: bp_chat_screenshot.png (image), access_denial_timestamp.txt (log snippet)", "From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Beth King <beth.king@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: possible retaliation after security report

Beth —

Thank you for flagging this and for sharing the artifacts. I’m the People Ops lead handling vendor-facing escalations. I confirm receipt and we take allegations of retaliation very seriously.

Immediate actions we will take:
- Preserve related logs and Slack history (we've initiated a hold on the workspace snapshot).
- Temporarily pause any admin changes by the involved Redwood account until we complete intake.
- Assign a neutral investigator from People Ops and notify Legal (copied).

Next steps for you: please share any additional messages or timestamps, and anonymize anything you cannot share publicly. We will treat this as confidential — we will not disclose Anya’s identity internally beyond the minimal investigator group without her consent.

I’ve copied Laura and Marcus to coordinate evidence collection and legal considerations. Expect a short intake form from me in the next hour.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior People Operations Manager
Redwood Inference", "From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: possible retaliation after security report — investigation logistics & privacy safeguards

Team —

BrightPath Health reported an allegation that Rishi removed a vendor contact's access after they raised a security concern. Initial artifacts: bp_chat_screenshot.png, access_denial_timestamp.txt.

Proposed immediate protocol (please action by EOD):
1) Preserve: Marcus — take a full snapshot of the BrightPath workspace, export Slack thread, and copy workspace access logs to secure evidence storage. (Attachment: evidence_checklist.csv)
2) Pause: Markus — temporarily restrict Rishi's ability to change external vendor access or modify the BrightPath integration until cleared.
3) Intake: Laura — confirm whether Legal needs to open a privileged review and advise on vendor notice language.
4) Investigator: I will lead the intake and do an initial fact-gathering interview with Anya (BrightPath) and Rishi. Please do not discuss the case outside this thread.

Note on confidentiality: treat all materials as highly confidential. Do not forward evidence to non-involved parties. I will circulate an internal no-retaliation notice to the small group and Rishi’s manager.

Attachments: intake_form.pdf (HR intake form), evidence_checklist.csv

— Hannah
", 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: possible retaliation after security report — investigation logistics & privacy safeguards

Hannah,

I want to be clear: I did revoke a specific workspace token because the BrightPath integration was causing a production incident; access was removed to protect customer data. I did not intend to punish anyone for raising a concern. If BrightPath has screenshots, please share timestamps and I will provide my changelog and rationale.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior DevOps Engineer
Redwood Inference
', 'From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: possible retaliation after security report — investigation logistics & privacy safeguards

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick response and for offering your changelog. At this stage please:
- Do not alter any BrightPath-facing tokens, workspace configs, or logs.
- Preserve your local and deployment change records and any Slack messages related to the incident.
- Send the changelog and any full timestamps to Marcus in the secure evidence folder.

We will treat your explanation as part of the investigation. Reminder: do not discuss the matter with Anya or external contacts; keep communications within this group.

I will confirm evidence collected by 5pm PT and schedule a brief intake interview tomorrow.

— Hannah
']
